name: verify-loop
description: Verify Loop: one place to verify a change or claim. It writes a check that can fail, loops until the check passes, keeps the proof, and returns a fixed answer (verdict, VERIFY: line, observed rejection, gaps). Users, skills and agents can all call it. Create mode generates a project /verify skill; maintain mode keeps it honest as the app changes. Also ships feature-map (manual-only): a FEATURES.md of every feature, its entry points and traces, checked against the code and linked to VERIFY.md. And latent-audit (manual-only): a dead-code cleanup held to three stages (a snapshot that records what each command really imports, in-place deletion of only never-loaded code with every command rerun, a verdict for every suspect left). And wire-check (manual-only): is code connected to the running system? A call-trace snapshot of every way in records which functions really ran, every function nothing entered gets a classified verdict, and a component you connect is kept connected by a FEATURES.md trace and a VERIFY.md check seen red on the broken wiring. And debug-protocol (manual-only): the root cause proven both ways, the failure reproduced on demand and gone with only the cause taken out, then the tree left as it was or fixed at the cause and held by a check that fails with the cause put back. And structure-gate (manual-only): is it spaghetti, measured? The share of code a parser actually entered comes first, every region no parser entered (code in a string, a language with no parser here) gets a counted reading or UNKNOWN, every finding gets its cost, and a `no` verdict is refused over code no linter or test can reach. And threat-model (manual-only): what an attacker can make the system do, worst first. A scan counts every way in (route tables, registering decorators, handlers, scripts), each one is attacked or shown to have nothing behind it, and each attack is kept as a test the suite runs; a fix must shut every open attack and fail again with the change put back. And evolve-maintain (manual-only): change a running system without breaking it. The tree as it was is kept and the commands users and jobs run are recorded on it, every function or config line that reads a name the change touched must be entered by a recorded run or given a reason, and every recorded command must print and write on the changed tree what it did before, unless the difference is one the user asked for. And perf-optimize (manual-only): make it measurably faster. The work is timed and profiled on the code as it was at two sizes, a change is kept only when the output is the same bytes, it beats the noise and a profile pointed at what it changed, and a guard left in the suite must fail with each changed file put back. And safe-release (manual-only): deploy, or change stored data, with a proven way back. The change and its way back are rehearsed on copies of the live data with today's code and the changed code: forward and its rerun, today's code on the migrated data (the deploy window and a code-only revert), the way back compared row for row, each loss named with the step that causes it; the live data is never written. And arch-design (manual-only): could the architecture be better? Where the structure costs the user, counted, shown as before/after pictures with the chain behind each problem, the top move written out with its landing steps, proof and door, the store or seam it is not adding, and a stop to ask which move to explore before anything changes. The install runs no hooks.
